w10_T4_001587: The Fenwick lighting depot received a shipment of 124 pallets. Each pallet was stacked with 8 crates, and every crate held 3 desk lamps. After the shipment was counted, the supplier sent over 18 extra lamps to replace damaged ones. Later that week a hotel returned 56 lamps it had never unpacked, and these went onto the same shelves. The depot manager, who has run the floor for a dozen years, wants a fresh count. How many desk lamps does the depot hold now?
w10_T4_001590: Ms. Alvarez started Saturday with 142 concert tickets in her folder. During the morning she handed 39 of them to the school choir for free. In the afternoon she returned 57 unsold tickets to the box office window. Every ticket she still had left was sold during the evening for 7 dollars each, and although her old ledger records amounts in cents she rewrote the takings in dollars. A patron who had bought a dozen programmes then added 73 dollars to her takings as a tip. How many dollars did Ms. Alvarez have at the end of the evening?
w10_T4_001595: A collector poured 212 glass marbles into 4 identical tins, dividing them equally so that each tin held the same number. Into one of those tins she dropped 70 more marbles she had found under the workbench, a bench that has stood in her shed for a dozen winters. Her nephew then borrowed 55 marbles from that same tin for a game in the garden. She afterwards filled 8 tins so that every one of them matched that tin exactly, marble for marble. The corner shop sells these marbles in bags of 39, and she prefers to weigh her collection in grams rather than kilograms. How many marbles are in those 8 matching tins altogether?
w10_T4_001601: A furniture workshop opened a carton holding 27 boxes of screws. Each box contained 6 packets, and every packet held 7 small cards. Each card carried 3 screws pressed into the backing. Over a busy month the workshop drove 2657 of these screws into flat-pack wardrobes. The foreman has been assembling wardrobes for a dozen different shops. How many screws from that carton are still unused?
w10_T4_001610: In the morning session of the trivia marathon Rosa played 4 rounds and scored exactly 142 points in every round. During the afternoon the judges awarded her 55 extra points for winning a tie-breaker, and before the dinner break she picked up another 66 points. Her teammate Dev ended the evening holding double the number of points Rosa had at that moment. A late correction by the scorers then added 75 points to Dev's tally. How many points did Dev finish the marathon with?
w10_T4_001613: A nursery began the season with 192 seed trays and sent 188 of them to its sister branch. Each tray that stayed behind held 7 pots, and every pot grew 2 chilli plants. A cold night killed 15 of those plants outright. Every plant that survived went on to produce 4 pods, and each pod turned out to hold exactly 5 seeds. The greenhouse where the trays sat is 38 metres long, and its labels give every measurement in centimetres rather than metres. How many seeds did the nursery collect in total?
w10_T4_001617: A food bank packed 211 crates on each of 7 collection days. Lorries carried 1185 of those crates away to village halls during the same week. Every crate still in the warehouse was then broken down into 6 smaller cartons for doorstep delivery. A supermarket sent over 54 ready-made cartons to add to the pile. The warehouse has 23 loading bays along its north wall. How many cartons is the food bank holding now?
w10_T4_001621: Priya began the month with 238 pounds saved up. Tutoring earned her another 37 pounds, and then a long repair bill took 272 pounds out of the same savings. A refund of 28 pounds arrived a week later. Her uncle Marcus, who compared her total with his own, promised to top her up until she held 5 times the amount she had at that point, and he kept his word. Her birthday brought 39 pounds in cards, and she finally put the whole lot into a scheme that returns 3 times whatever is placed in it. Her bicycle had cost 410 pounds when it was new. How many pounds did Priya end up with?
w10_T4_001622: A stationery depot opened the morning with 171 cartons of sticker sheets and sent 123 of them out on the early van. Each carton left on the floor contains 9 packs. At midday a supplier dropped off 11 loose packs to join them. Every single pack, old or new, holds 8 sheets, and each sheet carries 9 stickers. In the evening a customer returned 32 individual stickers still on their backing, and the owner, who has run the depot for a dozen years, wanted the full count. How many stickers does the depot hold in total?
w10_T4_001625: Omar's practice app logged 52 minutes of piano before breakfast on Monday. During the rest of that morning he added 16 minutes, and at lunchtime he squeezed in 8 more. The afternoon brought another 29 minutes, and in the evening he played for a further 73 minutes. The following Monday he repeated the identical routine, so that his combined total for the two days came to 2 times what he had played on the first day. The app shows his totals in hours, but Omar prefers to write them down in minutes. How many minutes did Omar practise across the two days?
w10_T4_001630: A small cinema ran 5 screenings on Saturday and sold 187 tickets at each one. Every ticket brought in 4 dollars at the door. The projectionist and the two ushers were paid a combined 1377 dollars for the day out of those takings. Film hire and electricity came to another 1686 dollars from the same money. The till prints its figures in cents, though the manager copies them into her book as dollars. How many dollars were left from Saturday's takings?
w10_T4_001632: Leah baked 102 muffins on each of 7 mornings for the school fair. Her friend Tom, who baked rather fewer than she did, handed over 25 muffins of his own for the same table. A neighbour added 69 more to the pile. Customers bought 144 muffins on the opening day, and a late delivery of 54 arrived that evening. On the second day another 261 muffins were sold from the table. The recipe card gives its oven time in minutes rather than hours, and the fair itself ran for 12 hours. How many muffins are left on Leah's table?
w10_T4_001636: Mr. Okafor counted 193 sticker sheets in the supply cupboard and threw out 4 that were water-damaged. He split the rest equally between 3 classes, so each class received the same number of sheets. Ms. Bell's class, which received exactly as many as the others, then gave 20 of its sheets to the nursery. Every sheet still with Ms. Bell's class is printed with 6 rows, and each row holds 5 stickers. The same cupboard also contains 84 spare rulers. How many stickers does Ms. Bell's class have?
w10_T4_001637: A sweet shop's storeroom has 32 shelves, and each shelf was stacked with 7 boxes. Over the summer 160 of those boxes were sold across the counter. Another 45 boxes went back to the supplier because their seals were broken. Every box that remains contains 9 paper bags, and each bag holds 9 toffees. The owner has used the same toffee recipe for a dozen years. How many toffees are still in the storeroom?
w10_T4_001639: A party planner arrived with 127 balloons and used 124 of them on the archway at the entrance. A helper brought over 6 spare balloons from the van, and the shop next door donated 27 more. The planner tied all of the loose balloons into 4 equal bunches for the buffet tables. The second hall needed twice as many balloons as one of those bunches held, so she prepared exactly that many for it. Her order form lists helium in litres rather than cubic metres. How many balloons did she prepare for the second hall?
w10_T4_001640: A scout troop collected 53 tins of pencils for a school appeal. They handed 30 of those tins to a shelter across town. Over the following week the number of tins the troop was holding doubled. Every tin in their store contains 9 pencils. A teacher then dropped off 15 loose pencils to go with them. The troop's log records meeting times in minutes instead of hours. How many pencils does the troop have altogether?
w10_T4_001644: A community centre stored 115 boxes of leaflets, and every box held 6 bundles. Each bundle was made up of 6 leaflets. A volunteer added 39 loose leaflets that had been left on the counter. Over the campaign 2664 leaflets were pushed through letterboxes. Two later deliveries brought 14 and then 22 more leaflets back to the centre. The opening hours on the noticeboard are written in minutes rather than hours. How many leaflets does the centre have now?
w10_T4_001646: Ana raised 46 tomato seedlings in her greenhouse, and her neighbour Ben raised twice as many as she did. Ben then bought 72 more seedlings at the market to go with his own. He planted the whole lot in 4 equal rows along his allotment. Every seedling in the first row gave him 9 tomatoes, and a friend handed him another 61 tomatoes from her own plot. Ben sold every tomato he had for 6 pence each, writing the takings in his book in pence rather than pounds. How many pence did Ben take in?
w10_T4_001652: A charity drive began the day with 139 tins of biscuits on the trestle table. A local bakery added 20 tins, a school class brought 26, and a delivery van dropped off another 50. Every one of the tins on that table holds 7 biscuits. At the close of the drive a sponsor matched the entire collection, so the number of biscuits was doubled. The organisers time their collection rounds in minutes rather than hours. How many biscuits did the drive finish with?
w10_T4_001659: Dario's market stall took 130 dollars on each of 7 trading days. He paid 577 dollars to his wholesaler out of that money. A supplier then refunded him 56 dollars for a crate that never arrived. The stall's rent for the fortnight came to 275 dollars, which he also paid from the same pot. He put everything that was left into a co-operative scheme that returns 4 dollars for each dollar invested, and it paid out in full. His stall is number 18 in the row. How many dollars did Dario end up with?
w10_T4_001660: A swimming club had 57 members registered at the start of April. A poster campaign brought in 55 new members during that month. Then 6 members moved away, and 19 more signed up after the open day. When the club merged with a neighbouring team, its membership doubled overnight. The club's timetable lists every session in minutes instead of hours. How many members does the swimming club have now?
w10_T4_001673: Helen and Raj found 202 conkers under the big tree and split them equally between the 2 of them. Helen gave 71 of her own conkers to her cousins that afternoon. On the way home she lost another 11 through a hole in her coat pocket. Her grandmother then handed her 34 conkers saved from the previous autumn. The tree they collected under is 47 years old, and Helen measures the string she threads them on in centimetres rather than metres. How many conkers does Helen have now?
w10_T4_001674: A cycling club's 176 water bottles were split equally between 2 storerooms. Into the first storeroom the coach, Mr. Idris, put 6 bottles from his own car and 36 more that a sponsor had sent. A weekend race took 102 bottles out of that same storeroom. Another 18 went to the junior squad on Monday. Mr. Idris then lent 6 more from it to Ms. Farrow for her school team. How many bottles are left in the first storeroom?
w10_T4_001677: Early in the morning a paper mill counted 158 pallets waiting in the yard. Each pallet was loaded with 8 crates, and every crate held 9 boxes. By the afternoon the checkers had opened the boxes and found that each one contained 4 packs. Every pack, they confirmed, was made up of 4 reams. In the evening a small van delivered 76 loose reams to add to the stock in the yard. How many reams does the mill have in the yard altogether?
w10_T4_001678: A bottling plant filled 162 crates during each of its 9 morning shifts. At lunchtime a partner factory sent over 43 extra crates. Through the afternoon two lorries took away 574 crates and then 614 crates. In the evening 68 crates came back undelivered and were put on the same stack. Every crate left on that stack was repacked into 3 shallow trays for the shop run. The plant's yard can hold 250 pallets. How many trays did the repacking produce?
